subdomain: 5.5 Address ethical AI considerations (bias, fairness, transparency)

en.question: A community information service proposes adding a minority language. Eight reviewed cases in that language contain no harmful missed escalations, while thousands of majority-language cases meet the release criterion. Policy requires demonstrated escalation performance for each supported language; a human-assisted route may remain available. Which three responses are justified? Select 3 answers.

options.text: Obtain appropriately collected, representative labeled cases with qualified language reviewers, including difficult dialect and mixed-context requests.
options.note: Representative evidence and qualified labels address the limited coverage of eight cases. Additional majority-language examples would not establish performance for the proposed language.

options.text: Report language-specific error estimates with their uncertainty and the high-severity cases that remain untested.
options.note: No observed harm in a small sample does not establish equivalent performance or satisfy every release criterion. Explicit uncertainty prevents absence of observations from becoming a fairness assurance.

options.text: Pool all languages and apply the precise overall error estimate to the minority language, since no minority-language failure was observed.
options.note: The pooled estimate is dominated by majority-language data and does not resolve the small subgroup's uncertainty. It can hide precisely the disparity the policy requires the team to assess.

options.text: Keep the proposed language on the disclosed human-assisted route until its release evidence is sufficient, while preserving feedback and escalation access.
options.note: A bounded supported route respects the stated per-language evidence requirement without silently granting unvalidated autonomous operation. Users retain a path to service and reporting while evidence is gathered.
